summary: This is a real step up from w8 (7.5). The flap now lies over the wing rims and reads as the dominant navy panel (flap / headrest-with-wings 0.55-0.59 in q13/q14, against 0.60-0.63 in py_37301/37302). The shell top is a continuous soft arch and no fabric shows above the rim from behind. The corduroy beat is gone: the vertical autocorrelation second peak went from 0.19 to 0.02 on q14 and from 0.23 to 0.06 on q13. The gooseneck is slim and smooth, and the lid meets the nose. Fabric colour matches the official photos within lighting: hue 220 against 218-222, saturation 0.20-0.21 against 0.21-0.35. It is not yet 'clearly the same product' because the headrest still differs from ANA's in the photos' most recognisable detail. ANA's wings are short, round, puffy EARS that stand well proud and end with a shadow above the backrest. Ours are tall flat strips that run straight down into the shoulder bolsters. The flap also reads too tall (rendered h/w 1.25-1.30 against 0.94-0.98), with rolled bar ends at the top and bottom like a scroll. The two stowed lamp heads hang parallel and touching, so they read as one grey plate, not two splayed silver cylinders.

issues.issue: The headrest wings are tall flat strips continuous with the shoulder bolsters, not ANA's round puffy ears. In py_37301 / 37302 / 37305 each wing is a short pillow with a domed top and a domed bottom. It stands about 4-5 cm proud of the flap face and has a visible shadow line under it, where the backrest continues behind. In q13/q14 our wing runs straight down into the bolster (the shoulder flare at y 0.62-0.82 merges with it), and its top is squared off.
issues.evidence: head_cmp: py_37301 / 37302 (left) against q14 / q13 (right). py_37302 near seat: the wing is about 0.70 of the flap height with a round bottom end above the flecked back. Render: the wing column continues to about y 0.45 of the back as one light strip.

issues.issue: The navy flap reads too tall, and it has bar-like rolled ends at the top and bottom (scroll look). Its visible h/w is 1.25-1.30 in q13/q14. In py_37301 it is 0.94 and in py_37302 (similar high camera) 0.98. The over-top piece and the 35-deg rolled side strips poke out at the top corners, and the hem band shows as a separate, more saturated strip (#1c295c against the body's #23305c).

issues.issue: The stowed gooseneck heads of adjacent seats hang exactly vertical, parallel and 1.4 cm apart, so in q14 they read as one flat light-grey plate with two black dots. In py_37305 each hose loops out from the shell side and its silver head hangs splayed about 30-40 deg off vertical, tip forward and down. The two heads are clearly separate, about 1.5 head diameters apart. From behind (q13b) the root bullets and heads read as chunky light canisters.

issues.fix: src/09b_py.js gooseneck: C = [[0.24, 0.84, zr(0.84)-0.065], [0.275, 0.80, -0.03], [0.285, 0.72, -0.10], [0.262, 0.675, -0.125]] (the hose bows about 4 cm out and comes forward). Head: hd = M4.mul(BH, M4.trs(sd*0.255, 0.635, -0.14, 0, 32*DEG, sd*12*DEG)), so it tilts forward/down and the two heads splay apart. Check the rotation order against M4.trs (yaw, pitch, roll); the goal is the lens end lower and forward. Head colour { c: '#b4b8bd', r: 0.2, m: 0.95 } so it reads as polished chrome, not matte light grey. Root bullet gCyl(0.015, 0.018, 0.06) -> gCyl(0.012, 0.015, 0.05).

Are these two lighting renditions of the same cloth, or do the back panels differ? We currently follow 37301 for the back and 37302 for the wings.
